name: Browser Vision
description: Lets agents browse websites through screenshots with an adjustable click grid.

command.name: bv
command.usage: bv open <url> | bv click @<n>|<1-9> | bv point <x> <y> — move the mouse to pixel coordinates in the screenshot (x across, y down, from the top-left corner) | bv point1k <x> <y> — move the mouse using a 0–1000 scale (0,0 is the top-left corner, 1000,1000 the bottom-right), whatever the screenshot size | bv click — click where the mouse is | bv type [@<n>] [--enter] <text> | bv type [@<n>] [--enter] (text in body) | bv select @<n> <option text> | bv zoom <1-9> [<1-9> …]|out|reset | bv view [--marks on|off] [--grid on|off] [--grid-color auto|#rrggbb] [--grid-opacity 0-1] | bv window phone|tablet|desktop|widescreen|<W>x<H> | bv key <Key or combo> | bv scroll up|down | bv back | bv wait [seconds] — wait for the page to change and settle (default 30s), then take a new screenshot | bv status | bv close
command.help:
Browse a website by looking at screenshots. Every screenshot result states
its size as image WxH. Marks, pointer coordinates and keypad regions always
refer to the most recent screenshot.

Aim in this order:

1. Marks. Every screenshot outlines the page's controls (links, buttons,
   fields, popup suggestion rows, …) with an @n tag, and the result lists
   them: [@7] button "Sign in", [@15] option "123 Main St". Act on a mark
   with @n.

2. Pointing, when what you need has no mark:
     bv point <x> <y>     move the mouse to pixel coordinates in the screenshot (x across, y down, from the top-left corner)
     bv point1k <x> <y>   move the mouse using a 0–1000 scale (0,0 is the top-left corner, 1000,1000 the bottom-right), whatever the screenshot size
     bv click             click where the mouse is
   The returned screenshot draws the cursor, and the result says what is
   under it: pointer: (412, 488) px = (322, 610)‰ — hovering option "…".
   Check the cursor and the hovering line before bv click; if the cursor
   landed off, point again, or switch between point and point1k. Pointing
   also opens hover menus.

3. The keypad, as the fallback: the view splits 3×3, numbered like a phone
   keypad (1 2 3 / 4 5 6 / 7 8 9). bv zoom <d> narrows the view to that
   region (chain them: bv zoom 5 3); bv click <d> clicks the centre of
   region d of the current view.

Every click reports what it hit, e.g. clicked button "Sign in".

Subcommands:
  bv open <url>               open a page (a bare host gets https://)
  bv click @<n>               click mark n
  bv point <x> <y>            move the mouse to pixel coordinates in the screenshot (x across, y down, from the top-left corner)
  bv point1k <x> <y>          move the mouse using a 0–1000 scale (0,0 is the top-left corner, 1000,1000 the bottom-right), whatever the screenshot size
  bv click                    click where the mouse is
  bv click <1-9>              click the centre of keypad region d
  bv type @<n> [--enter] <text>   click mark n, then type the text
  bv type @<n> [--enter]      click mark n, then type the body text
  bv type [--enter] <text>    type the text into whatever is focused
  bv type [--enter]           type the body text into whatever is focused
  bv select @<n> <option>     choose an option of a dropdown mark by its text
  bv zoom <1-9> [<1-9> …]     zoom into keypad regions, one level each
  bv zoom out | bv zoom reset back up one level | back to the full page
  bv view [flags]             take a new screenshot (keeps the zoom)
      --marks on|off          draw the element marks
      --grid on|off           draw the keypad lines and digits
      --grid-color auto|#rrggbb   keypad/mark colour (auto picks contrast)
      --grid-opacity 0-1      keypad line strength
  bv window <preset|WxH>      phone, tablet, desktop, widescreen, or e.g. 1024x768
  bv key <Key or combo>       press a key, e.g. Enter, Tab, Control+A, F5
  bv scroll up|down           scroll most of a screen
  bv back                     go back one page
  bv wait [seconds]           wait for the page to change and settle (default 30s), then take a new screenshot
  bv status                   url, title, window, view, settings, downloads
  bv close                    close your browser session

Any action (open, click, type, select, key, scroll, back, wait, window) returns
the full page again; view, zoom and point keep the current zoom.

Autocomplete: pick the suggestion's mark; if none, bv key ArrowDown then
bv key Enter.
Click into a field before Control+A; without focus it selects the whole page.
--grid off / --marks off hide the keypad / mark outlines when they cover
what you need to read.

Examples:
  bv open example.com
  bv click @7
  bv type @12 --enter         with body: search words
  bv type @12 search words --enter
  bv select @4 Canada
  bv point 412 488
  bv point1k 322 610
  bv click
  bv zoom 5 3
  bv click 6
  bv wait

Downloads land in /me/downloads/ and can be read or edited with the normal CLI.

Some sites block automated browsers. If a result says BLOCKED or SITE_COOLDOWN,
stop using that site, tell the operator, and do not retry or use other tools
(like curl) to get around it.
For property sale prices, public records are better and not blocked: county
property appraiser sites (e.g. Miami-Dade, Broward) and downloadable market
data such as Redfin's Data Center.
Browsing is paced per site so requests aren't back-to-back; paced lines are
normal.
